title: Kerala BJP leader P.C. George makes a U-turn in election funds misappropriation allegation
content: He says he had no knowledge of the actual election funds received in Poonjar. He instead accuses two local BJP leaders of misleading him into believing that ₹4.5 crore has been received for the constituency

content: BJP councillors allege disrespect to national song during Independence Day function, seek examination of video and CCTV footage

content: Emergency services, including in the Intensive Care Unit, Casualty and Labour Room in 19 govt. medical colleges in State likely to be affected; Andhra Pradesh Junior Doctors' Association says it was forced to intensify the ongoing agitation as the State government failed to respond to its demands

title: 12-hour surgery saves young man’s hip at Thrissur Govt. Medical College in Kerala
content: Complex vascularised bone graft procedure performed to preserve hip joint and delay or avoid replacement surgery

title: NTA to reconduct UGC-NET exams for English, Sociology, and Commerce after complaints
content: A senior official said that the decision was made after receiving many complaints regarding errors in the question papers

title: Pawan Kalyan issues alert on elephant movement in Chandragiri
content: The Deputy Chief Minister directs the Forest department officials to continuously monitor their movement and keep people in the nearby villages informed from time to time to prevent deaths and mitigate property damages

title: Row over Group-I only to divert attention from DSC irregularities, alleges YSRCP
content: The government is trying to politicise the issue without substantive evidence, alleges former Minister Adimulapu Suresh

title: Calendar offers a slice of Kerala’s heritage
content: A calendar brought out by a Thrissur-based cultural forum blends the old Vattezhuthu script, history and cultural heritage of Kerala in a unique annual edition

content: Parents question branding of absent students as ‘anti-national;’ SFI takes out protest march against school management

title: Children in Kerala’s Attappady get long-awaited bus ride, eye Parliament visit next

title: Tap potential of AI tools to drive projects and planning process: LSG Minister K.M. Shaji
content: Shaji said it was imperative that in the emerging scenario, it was essential to make use of technological tools such as artificial intelligence (AI) to drive projects and the planning process

title: Farmers’ march to Delhi stopped at Haryana-Punjab border
content: The Haryana Police, in anticipation of the march, sealed the stretch between the Khanauri border in Punjab and the Data Singhwala border in Haryana with concrete barriers and barbed wires

title: Man dies after son-in-law’s ‘assault’ over online gaming dispute in Chittoor
content: The police said Subramanyam had reprimanded his son-in-law for spending excessive time on online games; the man allegedly fled after the assault and a search is on

title: People’s Plan Campaign 2.0: student internships with local bodies proposed as part of year-long action plan
content: Local Self-Governments Minister K.M. Shaji inaugurates a daylong conclave of People’s Plan campaign activists

title: Journalists should learn skills to use AI, says seer
content: The field of journalism is changing rapidly due to the growth of digital media, says Sri Allam Prabhu Swami of Naganur Rudrakshi Math

title: Srisailam temple tableau wins second prize in Independence Day celebrations
content: The tableau showed the facilities for devotees, ticketing for darshan and sevas through ‘Mana Mitra’, and the temple’s outreach programmes in Chenchu settlements

title: Two screening staff injured as passenger’s gun goes off at Varanasi airport
content: The licensed firearm went off during inspection after the passenger declared it at the screening counter. A woman was injured in her leg and a man in his thumb and both have been admitted to a private hospital

title: Additional rice supplies planned if prices go up during Onam, says Kerala Minister Anoop Jacob
content: The government has written to the Food Corporation of India seeking its cooperation with regard to the additional supplies, says Minister

title: Lotus on the feast leaf revives a forgotten food tradition in Kerala’s Palakkad
content: The feast featured dishes prepared from different parts of the lotus, including the leaves, flowers, stems and rhizomes

title: Panel flags Meghalaya’s sloth on mine closure policy
content: The High Court-constituted committee slams the State government for repeated delays in cracking down on illegal coal mining and transportation and plugging the fossil fuel sources of coke plants

title: Only those who support Maoists, separatists are ‘dimagi Naxals’: Rijiju after Opposition's criticism
content: Addressing the nation on the 80th Independence Day, Prime Minister Modi on August 15 warned the country about “dimagi Naxals” who have allegedly entrenched themselves in the system and continue to pose a threat to society

title: Court tells LIC to absorb seven staff engaged under the guise of temporary employment
content: The High Court of Karnataka ruling may benefit similarly placed workers in LIC across the country, say advocates of the employees concerned

title: AP State Climate Change Cell suggests steps to mitigate impact on energy sector
content: Expecting a negative influence on infrastructure and methods used to produce and transfer energy, and discovering that the sector in a majority of the State’s northern and central regions is very highly vulnerable, the cell prescribes eight adaptation measures to combat it

title: BRS faults CM, Uttam pictures on smart ration cards, demands CAG audit
content: This exposes Congress double standards as it earlier opposed PM’s photo on Covid-19 certificate: Dasoju Sravan

title: Cauvery issue: Protecting farmers’ interests and upholding law both important, says D.K. Shivakumar
content: Chief Minister says if we do not follow the law, we may end up in a situation where control of the dam has to be handed over to the Central government

title: Minister announces ₹40 lakh for Nellore Vinayaka temple reconstruction
content: Ponguru Narayana performs bhumi puja, fulfils an election promise made to his constituents ahead of the 2024 general elections

title: Demand to install advanced screening systems in blood banks in Kerala to detect infections
content: This is in the wake of reports about the spread of HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C infections among college students in some parts of the country

title: Bangladesh sets extradition of Hasina, Hadi’s killers as conditions for Tarique Rahman’s India visit
content: MoFA’s official spokesperson A.K.M. Shahidul Karim said that “a propitious environment” is required for Mr. Rahman’s visit and urged India to “extradite” Ms. Hasina and the suspected killers of radical student leader Osman Hadi.

title: Keltron receives self-certification rights for three defence products
content: The products are an electromagnetic log used for measuring a ship’s speed, an echosounder used for measuring the depth below a ship’s keel and an underwater telephone system for ship-to-submarine communication

title: Bengal CM denies BJP's role in 'assault' of CJP volunteer, his father's death
content: CJP volunteer Shaik Abdul Hafeez and his family were allegedly attacked on August 13 after they visited a government school as part of the party's "School Thik Karo" campaign

title: Kerala Police initiate probe against educational channels that offer test paper clues
content: An estimated 40 lakh school students  are taking the Onam examinations, which will conclude on August 20. On August 16, the General Education department petitioned State Police Chief to conduct a detailed criminal inquiry into Instagram and YouTube channels that lure students by promising definitive clues about the mid-term Onam test papers

title: Jharkhand exam stir: Students to burn Rahul Gandhi, CM effigies on August 16; plan CM’s residence gherao
content: The students accuse JMM-Congress of playing politics; ask Congress to withdraw support from JMM-led coalition

title: Crisis deepens as service shortage hits rail passengers from north Kerala
content: Shortage of passenger trains and MEMU services between Central Kerala, Palakkad, and North Malabar blamed for worsening travel woes

title: Civil police recruitment exam: 141 OMR sheets go missing from Vijayapura exam centre
content: KEA has written to the Deputy Commissioner and Chief Superintendent of Examinations, Vijayapura District, seeking a detailed report on the incident

title: Bharath urges public to utilise free medical camp in Kurnool
content: A free medical camp is being held at Gauri Gopal Hospital on the 16th of every month for the residents of Kurnool constituency to mark the birthday of his father, former Rajya Sabha member T.G. Venkatesh

title: Over 2.37 lakh evacuated as Odisha braces for more heavy rain, IMD sounds red alert
content: Chief Secretary Anu Garg said fresh flooding had affected 5.15 lakh people in 947 villages under 331 gram panchayats across 49 blocks and five urban areas.

title: ‘Rahul, Hemant are dead’: Jharkhand protester performs ‘funeral’, shaves head
content: The protest by students and job aspirants over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations entered its 23rd day on Sunday, with the protesters, under the banner of JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, accusing the ruling JMM-Congress alliance of failing to take “concrete action” on their demands. They have also announced plans to gherao Soren's residence in Ranchi on August 20 and demanded his resignation.

title: IND vs SL: The ninety minutes! Moving day comes early in gloomy Galle
content: A rain-hit Day 2 in Galle turned into a frantic 90 minutes as Sri Lanka's bowlers struck in quick succession, dismissing India's overnight batters and bringing the hosts back into the contest. Devdutt Padikkal's 167 and a crucial lower-order stand kept India in control, but the pitch is beginning to offer the turn and bounce expected in Galle.

title: ‘He said it was unloaded’: 2 screeners recall Varanasi airport ‘accidental’ firing incident
content: Two cargo screeners were injured when a passenger's pistol accidentally discharged during security checks. The passenger claimed the weapon was unloaded before he pressed the trigger to show them. One screener sustained an injury to his left hand, while the other was hit in both legs. The incident occurred at Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport while boarding a flight to Mumbai.

title: US immigration authority: These forms will be rejected from September 15
content: USCIS will introduce new editions of immigration forms I-539 and I-765. These revised forms will be effective starting September 15, 2026. Applications submitted using older forms after this date will be rejected. This change aligns with a recently published immigration rule. USCIS emphasizes there will be no grace period for this form update.

title: Beyond bloodline: How donated milk is saving India’s most vulnerable newborns
content: Human milk banks in India serve a critical purpose by delivering much-needed nourishment to at-risk infants. Generous lactating mothers donate their surplus milk, helping those newborns who can’t receive it from their biological mothers. Every donation undergoes thorough screening and pasteurisation to ensure safety, highlighting the significant impact these banks have on the health of premature and sick children.

title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40B in medical debt; how mechanics work
content: MacKenzie Scott's donations have enabled medical debt abolition across America. Her model allows acquiring debt at low costs and then forgiving it. This approach has inspired other billionaires to contribute millions to similar causes. While philanthropic efforts are scaling, policy reforms for medical debt remain stalled. Scott's work highlights immediate relief possibilities and the need for systemic change.

title: ‘Unwanted record’: Ex-captain stunned after bizarre blunder by Pak at World Cup
content: Pakistan's hockey captain received a green card after gear was forgotten. This incident occurred during their opening World Cup match against England. The team failed to produce necessary protective equipment for a penalty corner. Former captain Salman Akbar criticised the lack of preparation and organisation. This lapse raises serious questions about the team's readiness for major events.

title: Solar-powered floating conveyor could handle 125,000 oysters a year in Maine
content: Engineers in Maine are developing an innovative solar-powered floating system tailored for oyster farming. This unique platform incorporates a vertical conveyor that efficiently transports oyster baskets from underwater to above, aiming to enhance production while significantly lessening the labor demands on farmers. Additionally, it aids in shaping the oysters and cleaning their shells from unwanted marine growth.

title: Elon Musk makes a promise to employees at townhall
content: SpaceX aims to enhance its AI model Grok by integrating insights from its workforce. Elon Musk envisions this initiative as a means to embed human values deeply into the AI's framework. Employees are not only invited to enhance the internal AI systems but are also inspired to share their expertise.

title: Punjab Police foils terror plot, recovers 690 gram IED
content: Amritsar Rural Police have effectively disrupted a potential terrorist attack aimed at a police establishment, recovering a 690-gram improvised explosive device. The Bomb Disposal Squad swiftly defused the explosive, ensuring public safety. In light of Independence Day approaching, security measures have been ramped up, and a case is currently under investigation to unravel further details.

title: Hockey World Cup: India hold Olympic silver medallists China to 2-2 draw
content: India kicked off their Hockey World Cup journey with a challenging 2-2 draw against China. Navneet Kaur opened the scoring, putting India ahead early on. However, Zhang Ying equalised with a penalty stroke. Deepika regained the lead for India with a penalty corner in the second quarter, only for Ma Ning to score in the third and equalise again.

title: ‘Going to go back to bed now’: Padikkal after career-best 167 in Galle Test
content: Devdutt Padikkal smashed his maiden Test century, converting his overnight 131 into a career-best 167 against Sri Lanka in Galle. The left-hander credited two years of hard work, clear plans against spin and confident footwork for his breakthrough. Padikkal also stressed staying focused after reaching 100, helping India reach a strong 460/9.

title: From burnt cash to possibly first impeachment: Justice Varma saga explained
content: Justice Yashwant Varma's residence was engulfed in flames, leading to the shocking discovery of burnt currency notes. A subsequent parliamentary inquiry confirmed serious charges against him, prompting his resignation. The Centre's pursuit of impeachment aims to set a strong precedential framework for judicial accountability. This case also poses critical questions about the interplay between a judge's resignation and ongoing disciplinary proceedings, potentially impacting future cases of judicial misconduct.

title: Padikkal falls for 167, joins Dravid and Pujara in Sri Lanka record list
content: Devdutt Padikkal's remarkable 150-run milestone during a rain-interrupted Test match highlights his growing prowess as a cricketer. He joins the elite ranks of Rahul Dravid and Cheteshwar Pujara with this achievement from the number three position. The match faced multiple delays due to weather, and despite losing Rishabh Pant and KL Rahul after resumption, Padikkal's performance stands out as a defining moment in his career.

title: Actor Ananya Raj dies: Family says she died peacefully in sleep; fans mourn her work
content: Actor Ananya Raj, known for '7 Hours to Go', 'The Final Exit' and 'Ghost', passed away at 27 on July 15 after battling physical and mental health issues for over a year. Her family shared the news on Instagram, calling her a "strong spirited girl." She also worked in regional films like 'Thaggede Le'.

title: 'Girls laugh, cry, then go numb': 608 flee Maha school amid 'mass hysteria'
content: Students fled a school in Melghat fearing spirits after experiencing laughing fits. Officials diagnosed the unusual behavior as mass psychogenic illness, a collective stress reaction. The incident highlighted existing management issues at the Doma village ashram school. Overcrowding and poor sanitation contributed to the students' anxiety and fear. Authorities plan awareness drives to combat superstition in the region.

title: AI Express flyer's pistol 'accidentally' goes off at Varanasi airport; 2 injured
content: Two security screeners were injured at Varanasi airport on Sunday morning. A passenger's licensed pistol accidentally discharged during a routine weapons check. The incident occurred while the passenger was preparing to board a flight to Mumbai. Both injured personnel received immediate medical treatment for their wounds. Local police are currently investigating the exact circumstances of the accidental discharge.

title: 'Human cost of relentless political hostility': Mamata on TMC leader's suicide
content: The former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee claimed that Asish Banerjee was "repeatedly maligned, falsely accused and subjected to relentless pressure". She said: The harassment and mental pressure he faced, despite his long record of public service, should make all of us pause and reflect on the human cost of relentless political hostility". Meanwhile, West Begal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said he would ensure probe into suicide.

title: UP officers invoke Bhagat Singh, Buddha to explain duty, justice and use of force
content: During the Independence Day celebrations in Uttar Pradesh, two officers reflected on public service and the importance of accountability. One officer referenced Bhagat Singh to address the frustrations surrounding the justice system's inefficiencies. The other drew from a Gautama Buddha story to discuss the responsible use of police authority, emphasizing that with greater power comes a duty to prioritize service over personal interests and mere salary considerations.

title: PV Sindhu turns to sports science, S&C in bid for record sixth Worlds medal
content: PV Sindhu won her biggest title since 2019 at the Japan Open earlier this year. There has been a gradual improvement in results and as she goes for a record sixth BWF World Championships medal, the focus is not just on what's happening on the court. The 31-year-old has turned to sports science and a strength & conditionining team to iron out the chinks in her armour.

title: Where are gold and silver prices headed next week? Fed minutes, Middle East in focus
content: Gold and silver prices may continue their upward trend next week. Geopolitical and economic cues will significantly influence this momentum. Analysts expect bullion to retain its positive bias amid global data. Investors will monitor US housing, trade, and inflation figures closely. Federal Reserve meeting minutes will also provide monetary policy outlook signals.

title: TMC leader's suicide: CM Suvendu vows probe into possible 'threat' angle
content: Asish Banerjee Banerjee was found dead on Sunday morning at a Trinamool Congress office in Rampurhat, Birbhum district. Police said his body was found hanging and was sent for post-mortem examination. The exact circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear. A teacher by profession, Banerjee had represented the Rampurhat Assembly constituency five times. TMC legislator Kunal Ghosh called for an impartial probe.

title: For 12 remote villages near China border, power is finally in sight
content: Remote villages in Uttarakhand's Johar Valley will soon receive grid electricity for the first time. This significant development will benefit approximately 180 seasonal residents and ITBP personnel stationed there. The electrification project, costing Rs 21 crore, spans sixty-one kilometers and includes twelve villages. Power lines have been laid up to Rasgadi, with Bugdiyar also slated for electrification shortly.

title: Market recap: Top 5 firms lose Rs 1 lakh cr in value; TCS, Reliance suffer biggest hit
content: Last week witnessed a downturn in Indian stock markets, with five out of the top ten firms experiencing notable decreases in market capitalization. TCS and Reliance Industries led the decline in valuations. In contrast, LIC and Bharti Airtel reported impressive gains. Despite these fluctuations, Reliance Industries held its position as the leading firm in terms of market value.

title: How members of England’s 1939 Chess Olympiad team became wartime codebreakers
content: As World War II erupted in 1939, England’s chess team withdrew from the Buenos Aires Olympiad. In Grandmaster Aarav Dengla’s fourth column for TOI, he explores how three players, Hugh Alexander, Stuart Milner-Barry, and Harry Golombek, returned home to join Bletchley Park. Harnessing chessboard skills like pattern recognition and strategic elimination, they played pivotal roles in cracking Germany’s Enigma code, helping secure Allied victory while keeping their wartime contributions secret for decades.

title: 'Awarapan 2' box office day 3: Movie set to cross Rs 70 crore on Sunday
content: The box office success of Emraan Hashmi's 'Awarapan 2' continues impressively, with the film crossing the fifty-seven crore rupees mark in India. On its third day, it grossed four point seven one crore rupees, bringing its overall net collection to over sixty crore rupees. It maintains a commanding lead against rival films in cinemas. Read on to know more in detail.

title: Cauvery water row: SC to hear Tamil Nadu plea against Karnataka on August 17
content: Tamil Nadu approached the top court on August 3, arguing that it was not receiving its allocated share of Cauvery water despite the state facing a rain-deficient year. The state government has alleged that both the quantity recommended for release by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee and the actual water supplied by Karnataka were far below its requirement.

title: ‘Very embarrassing’: Ponting tears apart Australia after Bangladesh shock
content: Bangladesh made history by defeating Pat Cummins' Australian team by nine wickets, prompting former Aussie captains Ricky Ponting and Matthew Hayden to advocate for significant team alterations. With the selectors facing mounting pressure to rejuvenate the faltering Australian side, Hayden proposed adding Sam Konstas and Matt Renshaw to strengthen the lineup. This match is notable as it marks Australia's first Test loss to Bangladesh on their own soil.

title: India cooks up LPG safety net: Govt fixes refinery-wise output targets
content: India is establishing production benchmarks for its refineries and upstream firms, aimed at fortifying the domestic LPG supply system. Reliance Industries leads with the highest targets assigned to its refinery. It is imperative that companies ensure sufficient infrastructure for LPG storage and transportation. These production benchmarks will undergo reviews and updates biannually.

title: "No BJP Connection": Suvendu Adhikari After CJP Charge Over Bengal Death
content: CJP member Sheikh Abdul Hafiz's house was allegedly attacked by BJP workers after he attended the Jantar Mantar protest and raised concerns over the poor infrastructure and mismanagement at a local primary school. His father died after the attack.

title: On Camera, Delhi Sanitation Worker Stabbed To Death, Colleagues Stage Protest
content: Following the incident, several MCD sanitation workers reached the spot and staged a dharna, demanding the immediate arrest of the accused.

title: "Country Won't Forgive": Amit Shah To Sonia Gandhi Over Vande Mataram Row
content: Amit Shah alleged that the Congress leadership showed utter disrespect to the national song at the party headquarters in Delhi, and demanded an apology from the Opposition party

title: Chaos In Delhi Metro After Paramilitary Official Allegedly Takes Woman's Pic
content: The purported video of the incident that went viral shows Delhi Metro passengers confronting the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel, who initially denied taking the photos.

title: "I Apologise": Man Who Wanted "Pure Veg" Client For Rs 6.5-Crore Mumbai Flat
content: Bhavesh Kaware made the apology after meeting Thackeray at Shivteerth, the MNS headquarters and residence of its chief Raj Thackeray, on Saturday.

title: Bangladesh Lists 2 Riders For PM Rahman's India Visit. One Is Hasina Return
content: According to a statement from the Bangladeshi foreign ministry, officials from both countries have been in contact for several weeks about the possibility of a bilateral visit by Tarique Rahman to New Delhi.

title: 'Flier Said Gun Not Loaded,' Recalls Varanasi Airport Staff. Then It Went Off
content: The passenger, Kamlesh Kedarnath Rai from Azamgarh in Uttar Pradesh, was travelling with his wife on Air India Express flight IX1810 to Mumbai. His pistol, a 7.62 mm weapon, had 21 live cartridges at the time of the incident.

title: Iran Executes Another Protester, This Time A Man Who Ran Over Cops
content: The number of executions in Iran has risen since the start of the Middle East war, which broke out on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes against Iran.

title: Trump Threatens To Hit Iran's Economy Hard. How He Can Follow Up
content: The Trump administration has varying degrees of closeness with all those countries except Afghanistan, but that border is mountainous and extremely difficult to patrol anyway.

title: Video: Apocalyptic Blaze After Massive Drone Attack Hits Moscow Region
content: A massive overnight drone attack in the Moscow region set fire to a Wildberries logistics facility, with visuals showing the warehouse engulfed in flames.

title: India Must Stop Seeking Foreign Validation: PM's Adviser Sanjeev Sanyal
content: On Independence Day, PM's Economic Advisory Council member Sanjeev Sanyal tells NDTV's Gaurie Dwivedi that India's real challenge isn't picking the right policy -- it's building enough flexibility to survive a world with no certainties left.

title: What Happens When Millions Of Young Indians Can't Find Their First Job?
content: Close to a quarter of India's youth aged 15 to 29 are what economists call NEET -- not in employment, education or training.

title: Air India Express Flyer's Gun Goes Off At Varanasi Airport, 2 Security Staffers Injured
content: The passenger, identified as Kamlesh Kedarnath Rai from Azamgarh, was travelling with his wife to Mumbai on Air India Express flight IX1810.

title: After Ambala And Hansi, Haryana Police Braces For Protests In Khanauri
content: Farmers from Haryana and Punjab are preparing to march towards Delhi against the proposed India-US trade deal.

title: Navy Sailor, Family Found Dead At Mumbai Home, Cops Suspect Murder-Suicide
content: Preliminary findings suggest that the sailor died by suicide after hanging himself, while the deaths of his wife and the two children are suspected to have been caused by poisoning.

title: Kiren Rijiju Shares 'Dimagi Naxals' List. 'Proud To Be One', Says P Chidambaram
content: PM Modi had congratulated the nation for successfully uprooting Maoists and also remembered the sacrifice of thousands of security personnel

title: Russian Escort Planted Trash Bin Bomb That Killed Ukrainian Defector: Report
content: Margarita Reut have been accused of carrying out the attack that killed Robert Shageev, a high-ranking Ukrainian defector who later served as an officer in the Kremlin's Black Sea Fleet.

title: "Deeply Value Friendship With Israel": PM Modi Thanks Netanyahu For I-Day Wishes
content: PM Modi also conveyed his gratitude to French President Emmanuel Macron, Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and Bhutan Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay among others for their wishes on India's Independence Day.

title: 12 Killed, 10 Injured After Tourist Bus Overturns In Hungary
content: The bus ran into a ditch and tipped over early on Sunday near the town of Mezokeresztes in eastern Hungary, police said, adding that the bus was heading towards the city of Nyiregyhaza on the motorway when the accident happened.

title: Over 100 arrested in Morocco over fresh Ceuta migrant crossing attempt
content: around 111 people arrested in ceuta for attempting another border crossing . the arrests came about two weeks after a large influx of migrants reached Ceutan . 109 of those arrested were from sub-Saharan Africa and two were Moroccan nationals .

title: CJP claims questions on youth protests, NEET, police action disallowed in Lok Sabha
content: DMK MP Matheswaran V.S. submitted three sets of questions to the union home ministry and the union education ministry . the questions sought answers on six issues: Refund of application fees for NEET-UG 2026 Growing public distrust in the government Denial of drinking water and sanitation facilities to CJP protesters in Delhi .

title: BJP lodges complaint against Sonia Gandhi as Vande Mataram row intensifies
content: BJP leaders lodge a formal complaint against Congress parliamentary party chairperson . the move escalated a political row over the recitation of Vande Mataram . BJP leader manoj Tiwari accuses the Congress leadership of showing discomfort towards the national song .

title: Bangladesh PM's proposed India visit conditional on Hasina extradition, officials say
content: the comments came as speculation grew over whether Rahman would travel to India later this month for his first official visit since becoming prime minister . he said that the necessary conditions for such a visit had yet to be established . Bangladesh has asked Indian authorities to "expedite their efforts to extradite Sheikh Hasina and other fugitives"

title: Can reputation of a celebrity be inherited, asks HC
content: the HC questioned whether a family's reputation flows down generations, how far personality rights extend and whether even "egregiously despicable" fake news can violate intellectual property rights . in 2023, a single-judge bench had restrained several YouTube channels from publishing misleading content on Aaradhya's health .

title: Bankim descendant seeks Sonia apology over ‘Vande Mataram’ row
content: BJP MLA Sumitro Chatterjee, descendant of bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, demanded an unconditional apology from Sonia Gandhi over 'Vande Matram' row erupted after a video from the Congress’s august 15 function showed Sonia gesturing and speaking to party president . BJP leaders alleged she was trying to have the rendition stopped after the opening stanzas .

title: At BCI helm for 14 years, Manan Kumar Mishra faces heat over professional conduct
content: a statutory body established under Advocates Act, 1961, is mandated to regulate legal profession and legal education . it lays down standards of professional conduct for advocates, exercises disciplinary jurisdiction, and recognises universities whose law degrees qualify a person for enrolment . but no provision of the Act gives it the power to admit persons as advocates on its roll .

title: 'Didn't call opposition leaders dimagi naxals': Rijiju on PM Modi's I-Day remarks
content: "dimagi naxals" referred only to those who supported Maoists and rejected Indian Constitution . "who want to cut chicken neck to separate North-East from India," he said . parliamentary affairs minister says the remarks are not meant for opposition leaders .

title: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act: Can new US housing law ease affordability pressure?
content: the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act is putting housing supply at the centre of the government's response to an affordability crisis . the law contains more than 40 provisions aimed at making it easier to build homes and expanding access to affordable housing . it comes as US home prices remain near record levels .

title: Tejashwi announces Raj Bhavan march over Bihar paper leaks, student firing
content: leader of opposition in bihar assembly announces protest march to Raj Bhavan . he says papers of recruitment examinations leak every time and a fair selection process has never taken place . "there isn't a single exam or recruitment drive where the paper doesn't get leaked," he said .

title: Walker Sisters sold Tennessee farm for $4,750 and kept a lifetime lease
content: the sisters, six unmarried women, refused to leave their mountain home . their story is one of resilience, independence and an unbreakable bond with the land they called home, as shared by the National Park Service . the family’s story began in the aftermath of the Civil War .

title: Iran moves to criminalise interviews with US, Israeli media
content: the broad framework of legislation would criminalise engagement with "hostile" foreign media . the bill's general principles were approved by lawmakers . details of the proposed legislation have not yet been finalised . a member of parliament's judicial and legal commission warned against treating reports as final .

title: Vande Mataram row: Shah takes 'sin' jibe at Sonia; Cong says 'diverting attention'
content: congress stepped up its attack on amit Shah after he alleged that veteran leader Sonia Gandhi committed a sin by stopping national song Vande Mataram midway at the party headquarters on Independence Day . the general secretary said Shah was demanding an apology from the Congress to divert attention from real issues and the government's massive failures .

title: Four Renaissance masterpieces stolen from Sicily museum in art heist
content: four works attributed to celebrated italian Renaissance painter Antonello da Messina stolen from a regional museum . the thieves reportedly bypassed alarm and security systems and escaped with four artworks . a double-sided panel depicting the Virgin Mary and the dead Christ in "Pietà" was removed from an armoured display case .

title: India gets seat at Nasa's Moon base table - what happens next?
content: the agency’s new Moon Base programme envisages a sustained human presence near the lunar South Pole . it is built gradually through robotic missions, crewed landings, commercial landers, rovers, power systems and, eventually, habitats .

title: Parliament at a standstill, protests on streets: The Monsoon session story
content: Parliament’s Monsoon Session played out on two different stages . the session was held from July 20 to august 13 . it produced an unusual contrast: legislation moved forward, but much of the political confrontation played out beyond the floor of the two Houses .

title: SAD chief Sukhbir Badal’s wife seeks NIA probe into Aug 13 attack, writes to Amit Shah
content: sukhbir Singh Badal was performing seva as directed by the Akal Takht . he was killed in the attack on her husband and chief of the sAD . the incident was "not an isolated one," the MP said .
